thread:
emma: Heads-up — starting bring-up for rwd-v5 v3.2-int4 (nf4 hybrid) as a gated canary. Want to capture both quality regressions and variability across slices.
noah: +1. what's your proposed traffic plan?
emma: start at 0.2% for 1 hour, then 1% for 2 hours if signals stable, then 10% ramp to 24h. auto-fallback if any hard threshold hit.
priya: what are the hard thresholds? can we be explicit so infra automates rollback?
emma: draft thresholds: 
- exact-match / concordance drop > 1.5% absolute vs baseline and p < 0.01 OR 
- MRR drop > 2% absolute on long-docs slice OR 
- hallucination proxy (n-gram novelty) increases > 3% absolute OR 
- tail latency 95p +50ms AND 95p error-rate > 0.1%
liam: couple notes: significance + absolute delta combo is good. for small cohorts, add min-sample requirement (n>=5000 requests per slice) before thresholds kick in.
emma: yep, min-sample for slice gating. also want a "variability gate" — detect high day-to-day variance that suggests unstable quantization outcomes. proposal: if rolling stddev on concordance over last 4h > 0.8% (relative to mean) then hold.
noah: agree. can infra calculate rolling stddev and flag?
infra-bot: auto-metric: rolling_stddev("concordance", window=4h) enabled for this canary. Alert route: #eng-ml -> paging if hard threshold + fast-fail enabled.
priya: we should shadow-run the float baseline on a 5% sample in parallel for the first 24h to decouple traffic noise.
emma: good call. config snippet I'm proposing for rollout policy:
```yaml
canary:
  phases:
    - pct: 0.2
      duration: 1h
    - pct: 1
      duration: 2h
    - pct: 10
      duration: 24h
  metrics:
    concordance:
      baseline: "rwd-v5:v3.1"
      min_samples: 5000
      abs_delta_abort: 0.015
      pval_threshold: 0.01
    mrr_longdoc:
      abs_delta_abort: 0.02
    latency_95p:
      abs_delta_abort_ms: 50
      require_error_rate: 0.001
  shadow_baseline_pct: 5
  kvcache_warmup: true
  auto_fallback: true
```
liam: that looks reasonable. How are we handling prefix mismatches and kv-cache cold start? those can inflate early regressions.
emma: enable prefix-aware gating: exclude requests with prefix_len < 20 from concordance check until kv warmup completed. also track kv_hit_rate; require >70% within phase to consider concordance stats valid.
noah: what about statistical test? use two-sided bootstrap on concordance with 1000 resamples?
priya: bootstrap is fine but ensure it's fast — run on streaming aggregates per minute bucket, then combine.
infra-bot: rollout policy deployed to canary controller. bootstrap_resamples=1000 set.
deploy-bot: canary started at 1724242424 on pool:dedicated-canary-3. Metrics available at https://console.redwood/inference/canaries/1724242424
noah: quick ask — add a noise-robust comparator: trimmed-mean concordance (10% trim) to reduce influence of outliers.
emma: added trimmed-mean check as secondary signal (trim=10%). if trimmed-mean delta > abs_delta_abort/2 then soft-hold (pause ramp) and notify leads.
priya: also add automated runbook link in alerts with steps to snapshot logs, rerun eval set locally and check QA prompt sets.
emma: done. runbook: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/canary-rollback
liam: we're good to go. small nit: record quantization seed & kernel version in canary metadata — we've seen nondeterministic delta across kernel builds.
infra-bot: metadata fields recorded: quant_seed=42, kernel=mmk-v2.7, compile_flags="opt-l2"
(deploy-bot) 1724242451: Phase 0 (0.2%) metrics: concordance delta = -0.6% (p=0.23), kv_hit_rate=48%, latency_95p +18ms. No hard abort.
priya: kv-hit low — expect warmup. keep an eye.
noah: 1724242520: Phase 1 (1%) finished: concordance delta = -1.7% (p=0.008), trimmed-mean delta = -0.9%. MRR_longdoc delta = -0.9%.
emma: that's over the abs_delta_abort (1.5%) and p < 0.01 -> auto-fallback should trigger.
infra-bot: auto_fallback triggered at 1724242520. Rolling back to baseline rwd-v5:v3.1. Canary halted.
deploy-bot: rollback completed 1724242550. Snapshot URL: https://console.redwood/canaries/1724242424/snapshots/1
emma: postmortem notes: apparently the int4 hybrid path increases ngram novelty for long-doc re-rank. need to run targeted quant-sensitivity sweep for attention kernels.
liam: add a controlled holdout (small slice) and run int8/float/quant4 variants to triangulate. also capture per-token perplexity distribution.
noah: agreed. next steps: run 200k evals across long-doc and rerank slices, test across 3 kernel builds, and prepare a modified quant table.
priya: I'll own the eval runs and collate slice reports. tagging @emma for follow-ups. :eyes:
emma: thanks all. closing thread for now — will reopen with results. :thumbsup:
